_meta.name: design-philosophy-outline
_meta.document_instruction: Write clear, authoritative design philosophy documentation for the Amplifier kernel. Use tables for comparisons, bullet lists for principles, and maintain a professional technical tone. Emphasize mechanism vs policy separation throughout. Avoid prose where structured formats (tables, bullets) work better. Keep examples concise.

sections.heading: # Amplifier Design Philosophy
sections.prompt: Write the document header with title, purpose statement, and use statement. Format: Title (H1), **Purpose**: (bold label with description), **Use**: (bold label with guidance). Keep concise - total under 6 lines.

sections.heading: ## Core Philosophy
sections.prompt: Write a brief core philosophy statement. Include the iconic quote 'The center stays still so the edges can move fast.' Describe Amplifier Core as an ultra-thin kernel (~2,600 lines) following the Linux kernel model. Explain it's a tiny, stable center with policies at edges. Keep to 3-4 sentences total.

sources.reasoning: Lines 1-8 contain the kernel definition, size (~2,600 lines), and the iconic quote about center staying still

sections.heading: ## Core Principles
sections.prompt: Document 6 core principles as numbered bold headings with bullet points. Format: **1. Principle Name** followed by 3-5 bullets. Include: 1. Mechanism Not Policy (with litmus test after bullets), 2. Ruthless Simplicity, 3. Small Stable Boring Kernel, 4. Modular Design (Bricks & Studs), 5. Event-First Observability, 6. Text-First Inspectable. Each principle should be concise.

sources.reasoning: Lines 9-24 contain the 4 core tenets that map to principles 1-4
Lines 19-56 contain 12 comprehensive tenets including Text-first (tenet 7), Observability (tenet 9), and Ruthless Simplicity concepts
Lines 19-25 define Ruthless Simplicity principle with KISS, minimize abstractions, start minimal
Line 8 explains brick studs and sockets (interfaces), regeneration philosophy for principle 4
